facts.claim: PEI's provincial heat pump rebates ended on April 15, 2026. A heat pump bought between April 15, 2025 and April 15, 2026 can still apply online for a rebate. Rebates are only available for one year after purchase.
facts.amount: No amount is stated on the page.
facts.eligibility: Heat pump purchased between April 15, 2025 and April 15, 2026. Apply within one year of purchase.
facts.dates: Rebates ended April 15, 2026. Page published June 30, 2026.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. Older efficiencyPEI documents list $1,800 for an income-qualified mini-split and $2,500 or $4,500 for a central heat pump; those amounts are NOT on this page and could not be confirmed, so no page states them.

facts.claim: Since 2018, the province and the Government of Canada have invested $95 million to install 45,000 heat pumps in PEI.
Free insulation upgrades for low- to medium-income homeowners: no upfront costs, no loans, free contractors and materials, expert advice.
facts.eligibility: Total household income under $55,000. You own the home. It is your primary residence (seasonal properties do not qualify). Tax assessed value of $300,000 or less. Wait for approval before any work; upgrades done before approval are not refunded. Apply in person at any Access PEI location.
facts.dates: No closing date stated. Page published September 2, 2026.
facts.notes: Read on 2026-10-21. Funded with the Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program and the PEI Department of Transportation, Infrastructure and Energy.

facts.claim: Rebates for homeowners and landlords for insulation, ENERGY STAR windows and doors, and air sealing. Rates depend on household income; households under $35,000 get the higher low-income rate. 1 SQ means 100 square feet. Rebate = SQ x R-value increase x rate.
facts.amount: Attic: $3.50 per SQ per R-value (low income $5.50), minimum total R50 flat ceilings or R28 sloped. Above-grade walls with new finish: $50 per SQ per R (low income $80), minimum increase R6. Above-grade blown-in walls: $10 per SQ per R (low income $16), minimum increase R10. Exposed floors and headers: $21 per SQ per R (low income $34), minimum total R20. Below grade: $21 per SQ per R (low income $34), minimum increase R12 walls, R20 headers. Windows, doors, skylights: $125 per opening up to $1,000 per property (low income $245 up to $2,000), ENERGY STAR v5 (2020 onward). Air sealing: 10% better $150 (low income $250), 20% better $375 ($650), 30% better $575 ($1,000).
facts.eligibility: Book an EnerGuide energy audit first ($99 plus HST, subsidized), do the upgrades, then a follow-up audit confirms them. Keep receipts. Low-income rate needs proof of income: the July Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit notice. The Energy Efficiency Loan Program may finance approved homeowners.
facts.dates: Rate table is headed 'As of June 2, 2025' on a page published September 2, 2026. No closing date stated.
facts.notes: Read on 2026-10-21. The page's worked example: a 30 by 40 foot, 8 foot basement from R0 to R12 earns $2,822.40.

facts.program: PEI home energy assessment (subsidized EnerGuide audit)
facts.claim: A home energy assessment from an approved company is required for Home Insulation Rebates. It costs a flat $99 plus HST; the subsidy is taken off up front. Book directly with the provider, not efficiencyPEI.
facts.eligibility: Providers listed: Clean Foundation, Homesol Building Solutions, RUGreen Energy Solutions, Sensible Home Inspections, Trinity Energy Group.
